content.title: UConn women's basketball's national championship history
content.text: UConn celebrates with the trophy after its 82-51 victory over Syracuse to win the championship game of the 2016 NCAA Women's Final Four Basketball Championship at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on April 5, 2016 in Indianapolis, Indiana. Connecticut won 82-51. Joe Robbins/Getty ImagesHere's a look back on the UConn women's 12 NCAA national basketball championships:UConn star center Rebecca Lobo exults after her team defeated Tennessee to win the NCAA Women's Basketball Championship on April 2, 1995 in Minneapolis. The Huskies won 70-64 to become the first undefeated champion in women's Division 1 in college basketball history.Matthew Stockman/Getty Images1995The one that started it all for the Huskies and helped increase women's basketball on the national stage with their first perfect season at 35-0. UConn defeated Tennessee during the regular season to reach No. 1. Senior Rebecca Lobo led the way for the Huskies, who beat Stanford then Tennessee a second time (70-64) to win its first national title. Lobo, captured in an iconic photo running across the Target Center floor in Minneapolis, scored 17 points and added eight rebounds in the championship victory.Article continues below this adGet Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.Get Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.ONLY 25¢UConn's Shea Ralph gets ready to cut her piece of the net after the Huskies beat Tennessee 71-52 during the NCAA Women's Final Four at the First Union Center in Philadelphia. Andy Lyons /Getty Images2000UConn and Tennessee met for a second time in the national championship with the Huskies prevailing 71-52. UConn finished 36-1, the lone loss coming against the Volunteers at Gampel Pavilion. Shea Ralph was the tournament's Most Outstanding Player and Kelly Schumacher had a Final Four record nine blocked shots.UConn's Sue Bird celebrates during the second half against Tennessee during the NCAA Women's Final Four game at the Alamo Dome in San Antonio, Texas. Connecticut won 79-56. Andy Lyons/Getty Images2002The second national title for the senior class that included Sue Bird and Swin Cash and the first for arguably the best player in school history, Diana Taurasi. UConn defeated Oklahoma to finish 39-0 and become the first NCAA team to have two undefeated seasons. There would be more to come.Article continues below this adFinal Four Most Outstanding Player Diana Taurasi of UConn participates in the traditional net cutting after defeating Tennessee during the 2003 NCAA Division 1 Women's Basketball Championship game held at the Georgia Dome in Atlanta. Connecticut defeated Tennessee 73-68 for the national title.NCAA Photos/NCAA Photos via Getty Images2003Not sure what's more incredible: the fact that UConn went back-to-back despite losing four starters from the season before or losing to Villanova in the Big East Tournament final to have its 70-game winning streak snapped. Either way, Taurasi led this group of Huskies, who beat old nemesis Tennessee 73-68 in the final, but had to survive Texas 71-69 in the national semifinals. Taurasi was named the tournament Most Outstanding Player for the second consecutive year.UConn's Diana Taurasi and teammates Barbara Turner and Maria Conlon celebrate after defeating Tennessee 70-61 in the National Championship game of the NCAA Women's Final Four Tournament at the New Orleans Arena on April 6, 2004 in New Orleans. Elsa/Getty Images2004The first three-peat for the Huskies, completed with yet another win over Tennessee in a championship game, this one 70-61. The Huskies finished 31-4 and lost to Boston College in the Big East Tournament. The Huskies also lost to Notre Dane, Duke and Villanova during the regular season. Taurasi completed her decorated college career by being named the tournament Most Outstanding Player for the second consecutive year. The UConn men also won the national championship.Article continues below this adUConn's Tina Charles (left), Renee Montgomery and Maya Moore celebrate a win against Louisville during the NCAA Women's Final Four Championship game at the Scottrade Center on April 7, 2009 in St. Louis, Missouri. UConn defeated Louisville 76-54 to win the national title. Elsa/Getty Images2009Five years almost feels like an eternity after such a dominant run. This championship was the first in the Maya Moore era as the Huskies beat Louisville 76-54 to complete the program's third undefeated season. Tina Charles earned Tournament MOP laurels thanks to 25 points and 19 rebounds against Louisville.UConn's Maya Moore (23) celebrates the Huskies' victory over Stanford during the Division I Women's Basketball Championship held at the Alamodome in San Antonio, Texas. Connecticut defeated Stanford 53-47 for the national title.Jamie Schwaberow/NCAA Photos via Getty Images2010A second-straight national championship and a second-straight undefeated season for the Huskies. UConn finished 39-0 just like the previous season. Most everyone returned from the previous season. Stanford led UConn 20-12 at halftime of the title game, but the Huskies came back in the second half to win 53-47. Maya Moore has a game-high 23 points and 11 rebounds.Article continues below this adUConn's Kelly Faris holds up the National Championship Trophy with her teammates after the Huskies defeated Louisville during the 2013 NCAA Women's Final Four Championship on April 9, 2013 in New Orleans, Louisiana. Chris Graythen/Getty Images2013After consecutive losses to Notre Dame at the Final Four, then three more loses during the season UConn beat the Fighting Irish in the semifinals en route to the first of four-straight national titles in the Breanna Stewart era. UConn annihilated Louisville 93-60, the largest margin of victory in a national championship game. Stewart was named the tournament's Most Outstanding Player after scoring 23 points and adding nine rebounds in the title game.UConn's Breanna Stewart holds up a piece of the net after a 79-58 victory over Notre Dame in the NCAA Women's Basketball Tournament Championship game at Bridgestone Arena on April 8, 2014 in Nashville, Tennessee. Frederick Breedon/Getty Images2014UConn defeats Notre Dame again, this time 79-58 in the national final, to secure a fifth undefeated season at 40-0, the most victories in program history. Coach Geno Auriemma passed Tennessee's at Summit with his record ninth national title. Stewart was again the tournament's MOP and the UConn men also won the national title that season, marking the second time the two programs had accomplished the feat. Stewart has 21 points in the final, with Stefanie Dolson adding 17 points and 16 rebounds.Article continues below this adUConn's Breanna Stewart and Moriah Jefferson celebrate on stage after defeating Notre Dame 63-53 during the NCAA Women's Final Four National Championship at Amalie Arena on April 7, 2015 in Tampa, Florida. Mike Carlson/Getty Images2015The Huskies finished 38-1, defeating Notre Dame 63-53 to complete the second three-peat for the program. Stewart won her third-straight tournament MOP award, the first woman to accomplish the feat. Stewart has 15 rebounds with eight points and four blocked shots in the final. UConn only lost at Stanford that season. UConn's Breanna Stewart, head coach Geno Auriemma, Morgan Tuck and Kia Nurse celebrate with the trophy after their 82-51 victory over Syracuse to win the championship game of the 2016 NCAA Women's Final Four Basketball Championship at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on April 5, 2016 in Indianapolis, Indiana.Joe Robbins/Getty Images2016The four-peat is completed, beating Syracuse in the championship game 82-51. It was the sixth and final undefeated season at 38-0. UConn's winning streak extended to 75 games, a streak that would end at 111 the following year. Auriemma passed UCLA's John Wooden with his 11th national championship. Stewart completed her incredible career with her fourth-straight tournament Most Outstanding Player award after a game-high 24 points, 10 rebounds and six assists.Article continues below this adUConn guard Paige Bueckers (5) celebrates in No. 2 UConn's 82-59 win over No. 1 South Carolina in the NCAA Division I Women's Basketball Tournament National Championship at Amalie Arena in Tampa, Sunday, April 6, 2025.Tyler Sizemore/Hearst Connecticut Media2025A nine-year national championship drought was hard to fathom, but that's where it was when Paige Bueckers delivered the Huskies their record 12th national title in her final UConn performance, finishing with 17 points. UConn defeated South Carolina 82-59. Azzi Fudd was the tournament's Most Outstanding Player, Fudd and Sarah Strong each led the Huskies with 24 points. Strong, who connected on 10 of 15 field goal attempts, added 15 rebounds.Score exclusive insights and analysis on UConn athletics.April 3, 2026Joe Morelli is a high school sports reporter with GameTimeCT. He coversr boys basketball, girls soccer and golf of all ages throughout the state, among other sports. He joined the New Haven Register in 1997 and has been with GametimeCT since its inception..
